1.o: After the introduction (ver. 1) the apostle begins with a thanksgiving to God for the saving benefits bestowed on them, ver. 2-5. And then mentions the sure evidences of the good success of the gospel among them, which was notorious and famous in several other places, ver. 6-10.
1.i: 1 Thessalonians 1 to 3 are the first letter Paul wrote that we have, and one of the warmest.
1.p: Lord, thank You for those who taught us to believe. Make us gentle with others, as Paul was with the church in Thessalonica. Amen.
1.l: Write or say thank you to someone who helped you to believe or to grow, and tell them what they did.
q: Paul compares himself to a nurse who cherishes her children. Who has cared for you that way?

2.o: In this chapter the apostle puts the Thessalonians in mind of the manner of his preaching among them, ver. 1-6. Then of the manner of his conversation among them, ver. 7-12. Afterwards of the success of his ministry, with the effects both on himself and on them (ver. 13-16), and then apologizes for his absence, ver. 17-20.
2.i: 1 Thessalonians 1 to 3 are the first letter Paul wrote that we have, and one of the warmest.
2.p: Lord, thank You for those who taught us to believe. Make us gentle with others, as Paul was with the church in Thessalonica. Amen.
2.l: Write or say thank you to someone who helped you to believe or to grow, and tell them what they did.
q: Paul compares himself to a nurse who cherishes her children. Who has cared for you that way?

3.o: In this chapter the apostle gives further evidence of his love to the Thessalonians, reminding them of his sending Timothy to them, with the mention of his design therein and his inducements so to do, ver. 1-5. He acquaints them also with his great satisfaction at the return of Timothy, with good tidings concerning them, ver. 6-10. And concludes with fervent prayer for them, ver. 11, to the end.
3.i: 1 Thessalonians 1 to 3 are the first letter Paul wrote that we have, and one of the warmest.
3.p: Lord, thank You for those who taught us to believe. Make us gentle with others, as Paul was with the church in Thessalonica. Amen.
3.l: Write or say thank you to someone who helped you to believe or to grow, and tell them what they did.
q: Paul compares himself to a nurse who cherishes her children. Who has cared for you that way?

4.o: In this chapter the apostle gives earnest exhortations to abound in holiness, with a caution against uncleanness, enforced with several arguments, ver. 1-8. He then mentions the great duties of brotherly love, and quietness with industry in our callings, ver. 9-12. And concludes with comforting those who mourned for their relations and friends that died in the Lord, ver. 13-18.
4.i: 1 Thessalonians 4 and 5 give comfort about death and a few short rules for living, some of the best-known in the New Testament.
4.p: Lord Jesus, You died and rose again. Give us hope for those who have died, and keep us ready for Your coming. Amen.
4.l: Encourage someone today who is sad or worried. Tell them one of the promises from this letter.
q: Paul says to comfort one another with these words. Who needs them from you today?

5.o: The apostle, having spoken in the end of the foregoing chapter concerning the resurrection, and the second coming of Christ, proceeds to speak concerning the uselessness of enquiring after the particular time of Christ's coming, which would be sudden and terrible to the wicked, but comfortable to the saints, ver. 1-5. He then exhorts them to the duties of watchfulness, sobriety, and the exercise of faith, love, and hope, as being suitable to their state, ver. 6-10.
5.i: 1 Thessalonians 4 and 5 give comfort about death and a few short rules for living, some of the best-known in the New Testament.
5.p: Lord Jesus, You died and rose again. Give us hope for those who have died, and keep us ready for Your coming. Amen.
5.l: Encourage someone today who is sad or worried. Tell them one of the promises from this letter.
q: Paul says to comfort one another with these words. Who needs them from you today?
